The '''[[artificial intelligence]]''' (AI) market in India is projected to reach $8 billion by 2025, growing at 40% [[CAGR]] from 2020 to 2025.<ref name="trade">{{cite web |url=https://www.trade.gov/market-intelligence/india-artificial-intelligence |title=India Artificial Intelligence |date=30 April 2024 |publisher=International Trade Administration |access-date=2024-07-20}}</ref> This growth is part of the broader [[AI boom]], a global period of rapid technological advancements with India being pioneer starting in the early 2010s with NLP based Chatbots from [[Haptik]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Madanapalle |first=Aditya |date=2017-10-10 |title=Inside Haptik.ai, a made in India and for India personal assistant and end to end chatbot platform |url=https://www.firstpost.com/tech/news-analysis/inside-haptik-ai-a-made-in-india-and-for-india-personal-assistant-and-end-to-end-chatbot-platform-4128927.html |access-date=2025-02-24 |website=Firstpost |language=en-us}}</ref> Corover.ai, [[Niki.ai]] and then gaining prominence in the early 2020s based on [[reinforcement learning]], marked by breakthroughs such as [[Generative artificial intelligence|generative AI]] models from [[Kruti|Krutrim]], [[Sarvam AI|Sarvam]], CoRover, [[OpenAI]] and [[AlphaFold|Alphafold]] by [[Google DeepMind]]. In India, the development of AI has been similarly transformative, with [[Artificial intelligence in healthcare|applications in healthcare]], finance, and education, bolstered by government initiatives like [[NITI Aayog]]'s 2018<ref>{{Cite web |title=National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence |url=https://www.niti.gov.in/sites/default/files/2023-03/National-Strategy-for-Artificial-Intelligence.pdf}}</ref> National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence. Institutions such as the [[Indian Statistical Institute]] and the [[Indian Institute of Science]] published breakthrough AI research papers and patents.<ref>{{Cite web |last=S |first=Raghotham |date=12 September 2024 |title=IISc scientists develop brain-inspired analog computing platform |url=https://www.deccanherald.com/technology/iisc-scientists-report-computing-breakthrough-3187052 |access-date=2025-02-24 |website=Deccan Herald |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2024-09-15 |title=IISc scientists achieve breakthrough in AI hardware |url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/cities/bengaluru/2024/Sep/15/iisc-scientists-achieve-breakthrough-in-ai-hardware |access-date=2025-02-24 |website=The New Indian Express |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Ramnani |first=Meeta |date=2022-01-27 |title=ISI director & AI researcher wins Padma Shri for contributions to science & engineering |url=https://analyticsindiamag.com/ai-news-updates/isi-director-ai-researcher-wins-padma-shri-for-contributions-to-science-engineering/ |access-date=2025-02-24 |website=Analytics India Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref> 

India's transformation to AI is primarily being driven by [[Startup India|startups]] and government initiatives & policies like [[Digital India]]. By fostering technological trust through [[digital public infrastructure]], India is tackling socioeconomic issues by taking a bottom-up approach to AI. [[NASSCOM]] and [[Boston Consulting Group]] estimate that by 2027, India's AI services might be valued at $17 billion.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Rajvanshi |first=Astha |date=2024-09-05 |title=India Is Emerging as a Key Player in the Global AI Race |url=https://time.com/7018294/india-ai-artificial-intelligence-ambani/ |access-date=2025-06-05 |magazine=TIME |language=en}}</ref> According to 2025 Technology and Innovation Report, by [[UN Trade and Development]], India ranks 10th globally for private sector investments in AI.<ref>{{Cite news |last= |date=4 April 2025 |title=India ranks tenth with $1.4 billion private investment in Artificial Intelligence: United Nations report |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/india-ranks-tenth-with-14-billion-private-investment-in-artificial-intelligence-united-nations-report/article69411505.ece |access-date=20 May 2025 |work=The Hindu |issn=0971-751X}}</ref> According to [[Mary Meeker]], India has emerged as a key market for AI platforms, accounting for the largest share of [[ChatGPT]]'s mobile app users and having the third-largest user base for [[DeepSeek (chatbot)|DeepSeek]] in 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barik |first=Soumyarendra |date=2025-06-02 |title=India's rapid AI adoption, China's open source lead in focus in Mary Meeker report |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/business/china-india-rapid-ai-adoption-open-source-mary-meeker-report-10043217/ |access-date=2025-06-03 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Meeker |first1=Mary |last2=Simons |first2=Jay |last3=Chae |first3=Daegwon |last4=Krey |first4=Alexander |date=30 May 2025 |title=Trends – Artificial Intelligence; BOND; May 2025 |url=https://www.bondcap.com/report/pdf/Trends_Artificial_Intelligence.pdf |access-date=3 June 2025 |website=bondcap.com}}</ref>

While AI presents significant opportunities for economic growth and social development in India, challenges such as data privacy concerns, skill shortages, and ethical considerations need to be addressed for responsible AI deployment.<ref name="carnegie">{{cite web |url=https://carnegieendowment.org/research/2016/08/india-and-the-artificial-intelligence-revolution?lang=en |title=India and the Artificial Intelligence Revolution |publisher=Carnegie Endowment for International Peace |access-date=2024-07-20}}</ref> The growth of AI in India has also led to an increase in the number of [[Cyberattack|cyberattacks]] that use AI to target organizations.<ref>{{Cite web |date=20 May 2025 |title=Nearly 95% Indian Firms Hit By AI-linked Security Incidents In Past Year: Study |url=https://www.businessworld.in/article/nearly-95-indian-firms-hit-by-ai-linked-security-incidents-in-past-year-study-557175 |access-date=20 May 2025 |website=BW Businessworld}}</ref>

== History ==

=== Early days (1960s-1980s) ===
The [[TIFRAC]] (Tata Institute of Fundamental Research Automatic Calculator) was designed and developed by a team led by [[Rangaswamy Narasimhan]] between 1954 and 1960. He worked on [[pattern recognition]] from 1961 to 1964 at the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]]'s Digital Computer Laboratory. In order to conduct research on database technology, [[computer networking]], [[computer graphics]], and [[System software|systems software]], he and [[M. G. K. Menon]] founded the National Centre for Software Development and Computing Techniques.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 2008 |title=Rangaswamy Narasimhan: Doyen of Computer Science and Technology |url=https://www.ias.ac.in/article/fulltext/reso/013/05/0407-0409 |access-date=31 January 2025 |website=Resonance |agency=Indian Academy of Sciences}}</ref> In 1965, he established the [[Computer Society of India]] and supervised the initial research work on AI at [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]]. Jagdish Lal launched the first computer science program in 1976 at [[Motilal Nehru Regional Engineering College]]. [[H. K. Kesavan]] from the [[University of Waterloo]] and [[Vaidyeswaran Rajaraman]] from the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] joined the [[IIT Kanpur]] Electrical Engineering Department in 1963–1964 as Assistant Professor and Head of Department, respectively. H.N. Mahabala, who was employed at [[Bendix Corporation]]'s Computer Division, joined the department in 1965. He previously worked with [[Marvin Minsky]]. The IIT Kanpur Computer Center was led by H. K. Kesavan, with Vaidyeswaran Rajaraman serving as his deputy. Kesavan informally permitted Rajaraman and Mahabala to introduce artificial intelligence into computer science classes. The computer science program was approved by IIT Kanpur in 1971 and split out from the electrical engineering department. In 1973, an [[IBM System/370 Model 155]] was installed at [[IIT Madras]]. [[John McCarthy (computer scientist)|John McCarthy]], head of the Artificial Intelligence Laboratory at [[Stanford University]] visited IIT Kanpur in 1971. He donated [[PDP-1]] with a [[time-sharing operating system]]. During the 1970s, the balance of payments deficit in India restricted import of computers. The Department of Computer Science and Automation at the [[Indian Institute of Science]] established in 1969, played an important role in nurturing the development of data science and artificial intelligence in India. First course on AI was introduced in the 1970s by G. Krishna. [[B. L. Deekshatulu]] introduced the first course on pattern recognition in the early 1970s.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=16 July 2024 |title=Artificial Intelligence Appreciation Day. Celebrating the Impact and Future of AI |url=https://pib.gov.in/PressNoteDetails.aspx?NoteId=151932&ModuleId=3&reg=3&lang=1 |access-date=30 January 2025 |website=Press Information Bureau |agency=Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=April 2022 |title=CSE at IITK: The DEC-1090 years. Remembering Rajeev Motwani. From IITK to IBM |url=https://iitk.ac.in/dora/spark/issue-3/spark-issue-3.pdf |access-date=30 January 2025 |website=The Spark}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Chandru |first=Vijay |date=2020-12-21 |title=The academic legacy of AI in India |url=https://www.historiansofthenow.org/post/the-academic-legacy-of-ai-in-india |access-date=2025-01-29 |website=Historians of the Now |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite news |title=Landscape of Artificial Intelligence / Machine Learning Research in India |url=https://itihaasa.com/public/pdf/LandscapeofAI-MLResearch.pdf |access-date=30 January 2025 |work=Itihaasa Research and Digital}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Sinha |first=Smita |date=2018-06-15 |title=Top 10 Machine Learning Researchers In India |url=https://analyticsindiamag.com/ai-features/top-10-machine-learning-researchers-in-india/ |access-date=2025-01-29 |website=Analytics India Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Foundation phase ===

==== 1980s ====
In the 1980s, the [[Indian Statistical Institute]]'s '''Optical Character Recognition Project''' was one of the country's first attempts at studying artificial intelligence and machine learning. OCR technology has benefited greatly from the work of ISI's Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Unit, which is headed by [[Bidyut Baran Chaudhuri]]. He also contributed in the development of [[computer vision]] and [[digital image processing]].<ref name="ieee2">{{cite web |title=IEEE Life Fellow Dictionary |url=https://services27.ieee.org/fellowsdirectory/getdetailprofile.html?custNum=wuV%2FRGDgNqLkDSNuwOHoig%3D%3D&bccaptions=Chronological&bclocations=%2Ffellowsdirectory%2FmenuCHRONOLOGICAL.html%3FbeginYr%3D2001%26endYr%3D2001 |accessdate=20 November 2018 |publisher=IEEE}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Unit |url=https://cvpru.isical.ac.in/content/computer-vision-and-pattern-recognition-unit |access-date=30 January 2025 |website=Indian Statistical Institute}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=A pioneer developer of Optical Character Recognition (OCR) System for Bangla and Devnagri script. |url=https://www.isical.ac.in/~cvpr/CVPR-WebSite/index.html |access-date=30 January 2025 |website=CVPR Unit |agency=Indian Statistical Institute}}</ref> As part of the '''Indian Fifth Generation Computer Systems Research Programme''', the [[Department of Electronics & IT|Department of Electronics]], with support from the [[United Nations Development Programme]], initiated the '''Knowledge Based Computer Systems Project''' in 1986, marking the beginning of India's first major AI research program. [[Prime Minister of India|Prime Minister]] [[Rajiv Gandhi]] requested that the Department of Electronics and [[IISc]] to initiate the '''Parallel Processing Project''' in 1986–1987. The [[Centre for Development of Advanced Computing|Center for Development of Advanced Computing]] eventually joined those efforts. IIT Madras was selected to develop system diagnosis, [[Indian Statistical Institute|ISI]] for image processing, [[National Centre for Software Technology]] for [[natural language processing]] and [[TIFR]] for [[speech processing]].<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":0" /><ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Saint-Dizier |first=Patrick |date=1991-06-15 |title=The Knowledge-Based Computer System Development Program of India: A Review |url=https://ojs.aaai.org/aimagazine/index.php/aimagazine/article/view/898 |journal=AI Magazine |language=en |volume=12 |issue=2 |pages=33 |doi=10.1609/aimag.v12i2.898 |issn=2371-9621}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=30 March 1998 |title=Supercomputer Unveiled |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/specials/supercomputer-unveiled-198033001036_1.html |access-date=30 January 2025 |work=Business Standard}}</ref>

In 1987, the proposal of [[N. Seshagiri]], Director General of the [[National Informatics Centre]] for the prototype development of supercomputer was cleared.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ninan |first=T.N |date=1987-11-15 |title=Government approves ambitious project to indigenously develop prototype supercomputer |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/magazine/economy/story/19871115-government-approves-ambitious-project-to-indigenously-develop-prototype-supercomputer-799502-1987-11-14 |access-date=2025-01-30 |website=India Today |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Singh |first=B K |date=23 November 2024 |title=Supercomputers: Tracing India's journey |url=https://www.deccanherald.com/science/supercomputers-tracing-india-s-journey-3288243 |access-date=2025-01-30 |website=Deccan Herald |language=en}}</ref> Negotiations for a [[Cray supercomputer]] were underway between the [[Reagan administration]] and the [[Second Rajiv Gandhi ministry|Rajiv Gandhi government]]. US Defense Secretaries [[Frank Carlucci]] and [[Caspar Weinberger]] visited [[New Delhi]] after the US approved the transfer in 1988. The sale of a lower-end XMP-14 supercomputer was permitted in lieu of the [[Cray]] XMP-24 supercomputer due to security concerns. The Center for Development of Advanced Computing was formally established in March 1988 by the [[Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (India)|Ministry of Communications and Information Technology]] (previously the Ministry of IT) within the [[Department of Information Technology]] (formerly the Department of Electronics) in response to a recommendation made to the Prime Minister by the Scientific Advisory Council. The '''National Initiative in Supercomputing''', which produced the [[PARAM|PARAM series]], was led by [[Vijay P. Bhatkar]]. For the first ten years, supercomputing and Indian language computing were the two main focus areas. [[C-DAC]] has expanded its operations in order to meet the needs in a number of domains, including network and internet software, [[real-time systems]], artificial intelligence, and [[Natural language processing|NLP]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Auerbach |first=Stuart |date=31 October 1986 |title=U.S. to Let India Buy Supercomputer |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/business/1986/11/01/us-to-let-india-buy-supercomputer/af0fcff7-cb2e-4485-b27b-de5d29625ef7/ |access-date=30 January 2025 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2004-06-06 |title=Reagan and India: Great Expectations |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/us/reagan-and-india-great-expectations/articleshow/722192.cms |access-date=2025-01-30 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Vasuki |first=S.N. |date=1989-03-15 |title=Indian supercomputer progresses |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/magazine/economy/story/19890315-indian-supercomputer-progresses-815885-1989-03-14 |access-date=2025-01-30 |website=India Today |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2005-01-13 |title=Target: Teraflops |url=https://frontline.thehindu.com/other/advertorial/article30203102.ece |access-date=2025-01-30 |website=Frontline |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Pitroda |first=Sam |date=2024-08-20 |title=Vignettes of working with Rajiv Gandhi: How C-DAC was set up in 1988 |url=https://www.nationalheraldindia.com/national/vignettes-of-working-with-rajiv-gandhi-how-c-dac-was-set-up-in-1988 |access-date=2025-01-30 |website=National Herald |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Shri Vijay Pandurang Bhatkar |url=https://msubaroda.ac.in/Distinguishedalumnidetail?id=194 |access-date=4 June 2025 |website=The Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda}}</ref>

Under the direction of Professor KV Ramakrishnamacharyulu from [[National Sanskrit University]] and Professor Rajeev Sangal from the [[International Institute of Information Technology, Hyderabad]], the Akshar Bharati Research Group was established in 1984 with support from IIT Kanpur and the [[University of Hyderabad]] for computational processing of [[Indian languages (India)|Indian languages]]. They focused on [[computational linguistics]], NLP with ontological database systems, and Indian language/translation theories with linguistic tradition.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Sangal |first1=Rajeev |last2=Chaitanya |first2=Vineet |date=2 August 2012 |title=NLP: A Paninian Perspective |url=https://sanskrit.uohyd.ac.in/felicitation/sangal.pdf |access-date=31 January 2025 |website=University of Hyderabad}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Department of Vyakarana |url=https://nsktu.ac.in/index.php/department-of-vyakarana/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241210232454/https://nsktu.ac.in/index.php/department-of-vyakarana/ |archive-date=2024-12-10 |access-date=2025-01-31 |website=nsktu.ac.in |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2022-05-28 |title=Celebrating Rajeev Sangal - IIITH |url=https://fac-webpages.iiit.ac.in/celebrating-rajeev-sangal/event/ |access-date=2025-01-31 |website=International Institute of Information Technology Hyderabad}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= |title=Dr. Rajeev Sangal |url=https://www.mahindrauniversity.edu.in/dr-rajeev-sangal/ |access-date=2025-01-31 |website=Mahindra University |language=en-US}}</ref>

==== 1990s ====
From IIT Kanpur, Mohan Tambe joined [[C-DAC]] in the 1990s to work on Graphics and Intelligence based Script Technology (GIST), which addressed the challenge of adapting personal computer software based on [[Latin script]] to [[Devanagari script|Devanagiri]] and a number of other Indian language scripts. He was previously working on the '''Machine Translation for Indian languages Project'''. Within C-DAC, he established the GIST group. The technology was expanded to encompass [[Natural language processing|NLP]], artificial intelligence-based machine-aided language learning and translation, multimedia and multilingual computing solutions, and more. GIST resulted in the creation of G-CLASS (GIST cross language search plug-ins suite), a cross-language search engine. The Applied Artificial Intelligence Group at C-DAC has developed some basic and novel applications in the field of NLP, including [[machine translation]], information extraction/retrieval, [[automatic summarization]], [[speech recognition]], [[Text-to-speech synthesizer|text-to-speech synthesis]], intelligent language teaching, and natural language-based document management with Decision Support Systems. These applications are the result of the foundation laid by previous language technology activities. Software firms in the Indian private sector began looking into AI applications, mostly in the area of [[business process automation]].<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=2009-02-12 |title=A success story |url=https://frontline.thehindu.com/other/advertorial/article30183690.ece |access-date=2025-01-30 |website=Frontline |language=en}}</ref>

In order to allow machines to read, comprehend, and interpret [[human languages]], the Language Technologies Research Center was founded in October 1999 at the [[International Institute of Information Technology, Hyderabad]]. It focused on the advancements in [[semantic parsing]], [[information extraction]], [[natural language generation]], [[sentiment analysis]], and [[Dialogue system|dialogue systems]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2024-12-10 |title=IIIT-Hyderabad's Language Technologies Research Centre celebrates its Silver Jubilee |url=https://www.deccanchronicle.com/technology/iiit-hyderabads-language-technologies-research-centre-celebrates-its-silver-jubilee-1845679 |access-date=2025-01-31 |website=Deccan Chronicle |language=en}}</ref>

Some of the early AI research in India was driven by societal needs.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Khemani |first=Deepak |date=2012 |title=A Perspective on AI Research in India |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/pdf/10.1609/aimag.v33i1.2356 |journal=AI Magazine |language=en |volume=33 |issue=1 |pages=96–98 |doi=10.1609/aimag.v33i1.2356 |issn=2371-9621}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=A Furtado |first1=Xavier |last2=Sen |first2=Aniruddha |date=June 1996 |title=Synthesis of unlimited speech in Indian languages using formant-based rules |url=https://www.ias.ac.in/public/Volumes/sadh/021/03/0345-0362.pdf |journal=Sādhanā |volume=21 |issue=3 |pages=345–362 |doi=10.1007/BF02745528 |via=Indian Academy of Sciences}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Agrawal |first=Shyam S |date=17 July 2008 |title=Development of Resources and Techniques for Processing of some Indian Languages |url=https://www.ldc.upenn.edu/sites/www.ldc.upenn.edu/files/agrawal2008.pdf |access-date=30 January 2025 |website=University of Pennsylvania}}</ref> For example;

* Eklavya, a knowledge-based program created by [[IIT Madras|IIT Madas]], helped [[Community health worker|community health workers]] deal with [[toddler]] illness symptoms by generating systematic case histories, offering basic treatment advice, or indicating when a [[Referral (medicine)|referral]] was necessary. 
* The [[National Centre for Software Technology]] (NCST) created the Vidya language teaching system, which enhances educational quality through the use of speech-vision processing, [[Machine learning|ML]], and NLP. 
* [[C-DAC]] created the Sarani flight-scheduling expert system.
* [[TIFR]] and the [[Central Electronics Engineering Research Institute]] created a [[Formant Synthesis|formant]]-based speech synthesis system for the [[Indian Railways]]. 
* [[IISc]] and [[ISRO]] built an image processing facility that uses AI and computer vision.

=== Growth phase ===
Around 2003, [[language technology]], [[computer vision]], and [[data science]] research groups were established at the [[International Institute of Information Technology, Hyderabad]]. With an emphasis on applied and translational research, the institute has the largest group of AI and machine learning researchers in India as of 2023. They also work on blockchain and [[quantum computing]]. In partnership with [[Intel]], they created the Indian Driving Dataset, which contains the largest amount of road data for unstructured driving situations worldwide.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chakraborty |first=Pradeep |title=IIIT-Hyderabad has the largest group in AI and machine learning in India: Prof. P.J. Narayanan |url=https://www.dqindia.com/iiit-hyderabad-has-the-largest-group-in-ai-and-machine-learning-in-india-prof-p-j-narayanan/ |access-date=2025-02-07 |website=Dataquest |language=en}}</ref>

The [[Government of Karnataka]] established the Machine Intelligence & Robotics CoE (MINRO) at the [[International Institute of Information Technology, Bengaluru]] in 2018 with the goal of creating frameworks and regulations for ethical and responsible AI technologies.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2018-03-02 |title=Siddaramaiah brings technology innovation under single umbrella |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/info-tech/siddaramaiah-brings-technology-innovation-under-single-umbrella/article22911123.ece |access-date=2025-02-18 |website=BusinessLine |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Machine Intelligence and Robotics (CoE-MINRO) |url=https://eitbt.karnataka.gov.in/it/public/129/minro-%28machine-intelligence-and-robotics%29/en |access-date=18 February 2025 |website=Department of Information Technology, Government of Karnataka}}</ref> It researches on [[human-machine interface]], [[Industrial robot|industrial robotics]] and [[automation]], data science and analysis, pattern recognition, [[machine intelligence]], and AI systems.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Raj |first=Gopika |date=2024-05-06 |title=7 Best Data Science and AI Institutes in India - Top IITs 2024 |url=https://analyticsindiamag.com/deep-tech/7-leading-data-science-and-ai-institutes-in-india/ |access-date=2025-02-18 |website=Analytics India Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref>

On 7 September 2018, [[NITI Aayog]], [[Intel]], and [[TIFR]] announced their intention to establish [[International Center for Transformative Artificial Intelligence]] (ICTAI) in [[Bengaluru]] to support applied research. Under the National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence, it will create and implement AI-led application-based research projects on AI foundational frameworks, tools, and assets, such as curated datasets and distinctive AI algorithms in smart mobility, healthcare, and agriculture.<ref>{{Cite news |date=11 September 2018 |title=NITI Aayog, Intel and TIFR collaborate to set up a Model International Center for Transformative AI (ICTAI) |url=https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=183377 |access-date=5 June 2025 |work=[[Press Information Bureau]] |agency=NITI Aayog, Government of India.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Waxman |first=Derek |date=2018-09-11 |title=NITI Aayog, TIFR and Intel Establish International Center for Transformative Artificial Intelligence |url=https://community.intel.com/t5/Blogs/Intel/Policy-Intel/NITI-Aayog-TIFR-and-Intel-Establish-International-Center-for/post/1333053 |access-date=2025-06-05 |website=community.intel.com |language=en}}</ref> On 16 November 2018, the [[Government of Maharashtra|Government of Maharastra]] signed [[MoU]] with the NITI Aayog and [[Wadhwani Institute for Artificial Intelligence]] to launch ICTAI for [[Rural health care in India|rural healthcare]] in collaboration with [[PATH (global health organization)|PATH]], Lords Education and Health Society, Wadhwani Initiative for Sustainable Healthcare, [[IIT Madras]], [[Sir Ratan Tata Trust]], and Stanford Center for Population Health Sciences. It will prioritize study, diagnosis, and treatment of illnesses such as [[Tuberculosis in India|tuberculosis]] and [[cancer]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=16 November 2018 |title=Maharashtra Govt. launches AI Centre for rural healthcare |url=https://www.biospectrumindia.com/news/98/12041/maharashtra-govt-launches-ai-centre-for-rural-healthcare.html |access-date=2025-06-05 |website=biospectrumindia.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-11-14 |title=Mumbai: Artificial Intelligence centre for rural healthcare launched |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/mumbai/mumbai-artificial-intelligence-centre-for-rural-healthcare-launched-5445104/ |access-date=2025-06-05 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}}</ref> 

NITI Aayog signed partnership agreement with [[Microsoft]] in 2018 to help expedite the use of AI for the development and adoption of local language computing, and to create [[farm]] advice services. Microsoft-NITI Aayog Problem to Solution Incubation Test Bed will be established. == Legislation ==

India currently does not have specific laws regulating artificial intelligence (AI). However, the Indian government has introduced several initiatives and guidelines aimed at the responsible development and deployment of AI technologies.<ref name="morganlewis">{{cite web |url=https://www.morganlewis.com/blogs/sourcingatmorganlewis/2024/01/ai-regulation-in-india-current-state-and-future-perspectives |title=AI Regulation in India: Current State and Future Perspectives |publisher=Morgan Lewis |access-date=2024-07-20}}</ref><ref name="indiabriefing">{{cite web |url=https://www.india-briefing.com/news/india-regulation-of-ai-and-large-language-models-31680.html/ |title=Regulation of AI and Large Language Models in India |date=27 March 2024 |publisher=India Briefing |access-date=2024-07-20}}</ref> The Indian government has tasked [[NITI Aayog]], its apex public policy think tank, with establishing guidelines and policies for AI. In 2018, NITI Aayog released the '''National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence''', also known as '''#AIForAll''', which focuses on healthcare, agriculture, education, [[smart cities]], and [[smart mobility]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 2018 |title=National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence |url=https://www.niti.gov.in/sites/default/files/2023-03/National-Strategy-for-Artificial-Intelligence.pdf |access-date=23 January 2025 |website=NITI Aayog}}</ref>

In 2021, NITI Aayog published the "Principles for Responsible AI," addressing ethical considerations for AI deployment in India.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-14 |title=AI Job Crisis: AI की वजह से भारत में सबसे पहले कौन-कौन सी नौकरियां खत्म हो सकती हैं? |url=https://timelybharat.com/ai-job-crisis-india/ |access-date=2026-05-14 |language=en-US}}</ref> These principles cover system considerations, such as decision-making and accountability, and societal considerations, such as the impact of automation on employment. The second part of this document, "Operationalizing Principles for Responsible AI," released in August 2021, focuses on implementing these ethical principles through regulatory and policy interventions, capacity building, and incentivizing ethical practices.<ref name="morganlewis" /><ref name="indiabriefing" />

In 2023, the Indian government enacted the [[Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023|Digital Personal Data Protection Act]], which addresses some privacy concerns related to AI platforms. [[Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology|The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)]] has also issued advisories requiring platforms to obtain explicit permission before deploying unreliable AI models and to label AI-generated content to prevent misuse.<ref name="morganlewis" /><ref name="indiabriefing" /> India is a member of the [[Global Partnership on Artificial Intelligence|Global Partnership on Artificial Intelligence (GPAI)]], which promotes the responsible use of AI through international collaboration. In 2023, the GPAI Summit was held in New Delhi, where experts discussed responsible AI, data governance, and the future of work.<ref name="morganlewis" />

Other Indian agencies, such as the [[Bureau of Indian Standards|Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS)]], are also working on AI policies. BIS has established a committee to propose draft standards for AI, focusing on safety, reliability, and ethical considerations.<ref name="dataguidance">{{cite web |url=https://www.dataguidance.com/opinion/india-ai-regulation-current-state-and-future |title=India: AI regulation - current state and future perspectives |publisher=Data Guidance |access-date=2024-07-20}}</ref> India has not yet enacted specific AI regulations. However, the government has introduced measures to promote innovation and address ethical concerns and risks associated with AI. These efforts aim to support the growth of India's AI ecosystem and ensure responsible AI deployment.<ref name="indianexpress">{{cite web |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/business/india-will-regulate-ai-but-not-at-the-cost-of-innovation-govt-official-9335211/ |title=India will regulate AI, but not at the cost of innovation: Govt official |date=17 May 2024 |publisher=Indian Express |access-date=2024-07-20}}</ref>

=== Hanooman series ===

The healthcare model VizzhyGPT is the first of these refined iterations, having been trained on extensive [[multiomics]], [[clinical research]], and [[electronic health record]] data.<ref name=":11">{{Cite news |last=Lohchab |first=Himanshi |date=2024-02-20 |title=SML in partnership with BharatGPT ecosystem unveils 'Hanooman' Indic LLMs |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/technology/bharatgpt-consortium-unveils-hanooman-a-series-of-indic-large-language-models/articleshow/107857921.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2025-02-27 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}</ref>

== BharatGen ==
BharatGen, formerly BharatGPT, marks the next phase of India’s sovereign AI development efforts. IIT Bombay Professor Ganesh Ramakrishnan thought of creating a homegrown solution that would use [[GenAI]] and take into account the linguistic and cultural diversity of India. An [[open source|open-source]], [[Multimodal learning|multimodal]], [[Multilingualism|multilingual]], India-centric [[foundation model]] called BharatGen was formally introduced on 30 September 2024. With an investment of less than {{INRConvert|235|c|lk=on|year=2024}}, the [[Department of Science and Technology (India)|Department of Science and Technology]] is funding the project under National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems. Due to security concerns in mission-critical applications like defense, the project gained strategic importance and aims to reduce reliance on foreign AI models. Professor Ganesh Ramakrishnan has been advocating for a [[Public–private partnerships in India|public–private partnership]] in AI through the Bharat GPT program. The earlier Bharat GPT efforts have taken on a more formal role in the BharatGen project, which is anticipated for completion by 2026.<ref name=":7">{{Cite web |last=Pandey |first=Mohit |date=2024-10-02 |title=Government of India Launches BharatGen, First Government-Funded Multimodal AI Initiative |url=https://analyticsindiamag.com/ai-news-updates/government-of-india-launches-bharatgen-first-government-funded-multimodal-ai-initiative/ |access-date=2025-02-26 |website=Analytics India Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Pandey |first=Mohit |date=2025-02-24 |title=This Govt-Funded ₹235 Cr AI Initiative is India's Real Answer to DeepSeek |url=https://analyticsindiamag.com/ai-features/this-govt-funded-%E2%82%B9235-cr-ai-initiative-is-indias-real-answer-to-deepseek/ |access-date=2025-02-26 |website=Analytics India Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref>

As a national mission, BharatGen has been set up to facilitate inter-ministerial cooperation by taking [[whole-of-government approach]]. The AI will be developed from the ground up, guaranteeing that all [[intellectual property]] stays in the country. IndiaAI Compute Facility will spearhead the project. BharatGen will have robust academic base, incorporating faculty and research institutions into its ecosystem to guarantee sustained innovation. [[Yotta Infrastructure]], and Neysa are providing [[Cloud computing|cloud support]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pandey |first=Mohit |date=2025-02-24 |title=This Govt-Funded ₹235 Cr AI Initiative is India's Real Answer to DeepSeek |url=https://analyticsindiamag.com/ai-features/this-govt-funded-%E2%82%B9235-cr-ai-initiative-is-indias-real-answer-to-deepseek/ |access-date=2025-02-26 |website=Analytics India Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Pandey |first=Mohit |date=2025-01-29 |title=India Will Have its Own LLM Soon, Says IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw |url=https://analyticsindiamag.com/ai-news-updates/india-will-have-its-own-llm-soon-says-it-minister-ashwini-vaishnaw/ |access-date=2025-02-26 |website=Analytics India Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref>

The [[Backend (computing)|backend]] [[algorithm]] development and the necessary technical work was done by a collaborative team from BharatGen consortium. As of February 2025, the BharatGen consortium has 50–60 researchers and a wide range of student contributors from the [[Indian Institute of Management Indore]], the [[International Institute of Information Technology, Hyderabad]], [[IIT Bombay]], [[IIT Kanpur]], [[IIT Hyderabad]], [[IIT Mandi]], and [[IIT Madras]]. BharatGen consortium will work with behavioral economists, engineers, AI researchers, and design specialists, to develop a multidisciplinary strategy to use AI to address India's problems. The AI model takes into account the 1,600 languages and scripts that make up the Indian knowledge system. Each institute of the consortium is investigating particular tasks to create models in [[Speech recognition|voice]], [[Language model|language]], and [[Computer vision|vision]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Pandit |first=Niraj |date=2024-10-04 |title=BharatGen geared to put a desi spin on ChatGPT, IIT-Bombay plays role |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cities/mumbai-news/bharatgen-geared-to-put-a-desi-spin-on-chatgpt-101727982824794.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241004070214/https://www.hindustantimes.com/cities/mumbai-news/bharatgen-geared-to-put-a-desi-spin-on-chatgpt-101727982824794.html |archive-date=2024-10-04 |access-date=2025-02-26 |work=Hindustan Times |language=en-us}}</ref><ref name=":6">{{Cite news |date=18 December 2024 |title=Parliament Question: Launch of BharatGen |url=https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2085534 |access-date=26 February 2025 |work=[[Press Information Bureau]] |agency=Ministry of Science & Technology, Government of India}}</ref> 

As of 30 January 2025, the framework for the AI model is ready. The development team has spent the last one and a half years working on the project. The initial version should be available in four to ten months, according to [[Ashwini Vaishnaw]], Minister of Electronics and IT.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Garg |first=Ankita |date=2025-01-30 |title=India to develop its own AI model like ChatGPT and DeepSeek in 10 months: Ashwini Vaishnaw |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/technology/news/story/india-to-develop-its-own-ai-model-like-chatgpt-and-deepseek-in-10-months-ashwini-vaishnaw-2672368-2025-01-30 |access-date=2025-02-26 |website=India Today |language=en}}</ref>

In order to concentrate on primary data collection, BharatGen started the [[Bharat Data Sagar]] initiative, a multilingual repository for AI research. The goal of this data collection is to satisfy the need for training data for Indian languages that are underrepresented in [[Data corpus|data corpora]]. It will capture the Indian linguistic nuances, which are frequently disregarded in international AI models. BharatGen offers tools and technologies to facilitate the creation of region specific tailored content by translating between local languages and dialects. In order to accurately portray India's languages, dialects, and cultural context, BharatGen focuses on gathering and curating data unique to the nation.<ref name=":7" /><ref name=":6" />

Using [[Computer vision|vision]] language models, BharatGen launched e-vikrAI in October 2024. It makes e-commerce easier for non-English speaking vendors by automating the cataloguing process and doing away with the need for human input. Sellers only need to provide an image of their product to get auto-generated titles, descriptions, features, and pricing recommendations. e-vikrAI improves accessibility by translating and vocalizing product descriptions in Indian languages.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pandey |first=Mohit |date=2024-10-16 |title=BharatGen Launches e-vikrAI, Vision Language Model for Indic e-Commerce |url=https://analyticsindiamag.com/ai-news-updates/bharatgen-launches-e-vikrai-vision-language-model-for-indic-e-commerce/ |access-date=2025-02-27 |website=Analytics India Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2024-10-25 |title=Two Hyderabad research institutes lead country's AI revolution with BharatGen's e-VikrAI |url=https://www.deccanchronicle.com/southern-states/telangana/two-hyderabad-research-institutes-lead-countrys-ai-revolution-with-bharatgens-e-vikrai-1833071 |access-date=2025-02-27 |website=deccanchronicle.com |language=en}}</ref>

=== AI Research Analytics and Knowledge Dissemination Platform ===
With a peak performance of 13,170 [[teraflops]], AIRAWAT-PSAI is the biggest and fastest AI supercomputing machine in India. It was deployed at [[C-DAC|C-DAC, Pune]] in 2023 and is maintained by Netweb Technologies.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-08-17 |title=India's AI supercomputer 'AIRAWAT' makes it to the list of world's '100 most powerful' |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/gadgets-news/indias-ai-supercomputer-airawat-makes-it-to-the-list-of-worlds-100-most-powerful/articleshow/100487763.cms |access-date=2025-06-04 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref> 

[[MeitY]] is also funding the implementation of 200 AI [[Petaflops]] [[Mixed-precision arithmetic|Mixed Precision]] peak computing capacity (scalable to 790 AI Petaflops) [[Proof of concept|Proof of Concept]] for AI Research Analytics and Knowledge Dissemination Platform (AIRAWAT), which is being carried out by C-DAC, Pune. A combined peak compute of 410 AI Petaflops Mixed Precision and a sustained compute capability of 8.5 Petaflops ([[Rmax (computing)|Rmax]]) [[Double-precision floating-point format|Double Precision]] are achieved by combining the 200 AI Petaflop AIRAWAT PoC with the 210 AI Petaflop [[PARAM Siddhi-AI]]. 13 Petaflops is the maximum computation capacity (Double Precision, Rpeak). A plan for expanding AIRAWAT to 1,000 AI Petaflops of Mixed Precision computing capacity has been envisioned by MeitY. With its extensive, power-optimized AI cloud infrastructure, AIRAWAT will serve as a common computational cloud platform for Big Data Analytics and Assimilation, linking all Centers for Research Excellence in Artificial Intelligence (COREs), Indian Centres for Transformational AI (ICTAIs), and other academic, research lab, scientific community, industry, and start-up institutions with the National Knowledge Network.

With an emphasis on [[NLP (computer science)|NLP]], surveillance and [[image processing]], [[pattern recognition]], [[medical imaging]], education, agriculture, finance, healthcare, audio assistance, robotics, national security, defense, the automotive industry, supply chain management, [[human resource development]], and anomalous behavior detection from [[video analytics]], AIRAWAT will support the field of applied AI. Deployed under the [[National Supercomputing Mission]], it will support the [[Digital India]] [[Bhashini]] initiative and accomplish the goals of the National Program on AI.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AIRAWAT-PSAI |url=https://airawat.cdac.in/airawat/ |access-date=4 June 2025 |website=Centre for Development of Advanced Computing}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=24 May 2023 |title=AI Supercomputer 'AIRAWAT' puts India among top supercomputing league |url=https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1926942 |access-date=4 June 2025 |work=[[Press Information Bureau]] |agency=Ministry of Electronics & IT, Government of India.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=27 December 2024 |title=Year End Review 2024 of Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology Part-1 |url=https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2088268 |access-date=4 June 2025 |work=[[Press Information Bureau]] |agency=Ministry of Electronics & IT, Government of India.}}</ref>

The [[National Pest Surveillance System]] uses AI and [[Machine learning|ML]] to identify pest infestation, allowing for prompt action for healthier crops and addressing the loss of produce brought on by climate change. === Internal security ===
To dismantle [[Organised crime in India|organized crime]] and [[Terrorism in India|terrorism]] networks, [[Ministry of Home Affairs (India)|Ministry of Home Affairs]] established [[NATGRID#Organised Crime Network Database|Organised Crime Network Database]] on 26 December 2025. Investigative agencies can utilize the OCND, an AI-powered advanced analytics tool to rapidly gather comprehensive information about terrorist networks and [[crime syndicates]]. Investigating agencies can instantly access [[First information report|first information reports]], [[Chargesheet|chargesheets]], dossiers, and other vital information about crimes from all [[Indian states]]. === Space ===
MOI-TD, India's first AI lab in space, is being built by TakeMe2Space. AI's potential utility in space will be demonstrated with the MOI-TD mission. In order to foresee natural disasters and comprehend climate change, the MOI-TD will assist with environmental monitoring, weather pattern analysis, and Earth's surface change tracking. The lab will process the data in real time, allowing for analysis of the information at the time of collection.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reddy |first=Anurag |date=2025-02-11 |title=Hyderabad Startup Building India's First AI Lab in Orbit |url=https://www.analyticsinsight.net/artificial-intelligence/hyderabad-startup-building-indias-first-ai-lab-in-orbit |access-date=2025-03-15 |website=Analytics Insight |language=en}}</ref> The MOI-TD mission showed that it was possible to run external code on the satellite, securely downlink encrypted data, and uplink huge AI models from a ground station through OrbitLab, a web-based console. It effectively validated key subsystems, including computer infrastructure (Zero Cube AI Accelerator, [[PSLV Orbital Experiment Module|POEM]] Adapter Board), actuators (MagnetoTorquers, AirTorquers, [[Reaction wheel|Reaction Wheel]]), and sensors ([[Sun sensor|Sun Sensor]], Horizon Sensor, Solar Cell, [[Inertial measurement unit|IMUs]]). The foundation for space-based computing is laid by MOI-TD. The creation of space-based data centers will be facilitated by the upcoming MOI-1 AI Lab mission. Support for the project came from the [[Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre|Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Center]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-03-05 |title=TakeMe2Space secures Rs 5.5 crore in Pre-Seed Funding to launch India's first AI lab in space |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/business/start-ups-takeme2space-secures-rs-5-5-crore-in-pre-seed-funding-to-launch-indias-first-ai-lab-in-space-3767831/ |access-date=2025-03-15 |website=Financialexpress |language=en}}</ref> One study by the [[University of Southampton]] on TakeMe2Space's AI lab used a low-power AI system to lessen [[Motion blur (media)|motion blur]] in satellite imagery.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gupta |first=Sanjana |date=2025-02-08 |title=This Hyderabad Startup is Building India's First AI Lab in Orbit |url=https://analyticsindiamag.com/deep-tech/this-hyderabad-startup-is-building-indias-first-ai-lab-in-orbit/ |access-date=2025-03-16 |website=Analytics India Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref>

The tool provides measurements like the proportion of lung size and volume impacted by the anomalies.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Bora |first=Garima |date=2020-04-30 |title=Qure.ai can detect Covid-19 lung infections in less than a minute, help triage patients |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/small-biz/startups/newsbuzz/qure-ai-can-detect-covid-19-lung-infections-in-less-than-a-minute-help-triage-patients/articleshow/75464679.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2025-02-08 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=6 July 2022 |title=AI, ML making equitable, high-quality healthcare a reality: Qure.ai |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/technology/ai-ml-making-equitable-high-quality-healthcare-a-reality-qure-ai-122070600388_1.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250123160438/https://www.business-standard.com/article/technology/ai-ml-making-equitable-high-quality-healthcare-a-reality-qure-ai-122070600388_1.html |archive-date=2025-01-23 |access-date=2025-02-08 |website=Business Standard |language=en-US}}</ref> The Computational and Data Sciences Collaborative Laboratory of Artificial Intelligence in Medical and Healthcare Imaging was established by [[Wipro]] [[GE HealthCare]] at [[IISc]] in September 2020. Its goal is to develop advanced diagnostic and medical image-reconstruction techniques and protocols for quicker and better imaging by utilizing deep learning, AI, and future-ready digital interfaces.<ref>{{Cite web |date=24 September 2024 |title=Wipro GE Healthcare, IISc set up health tech innovation lab |url=https://www.biospectrumindia.com/news/98/17265/wipro-ge-healthcare-iisc-set-up-health-tech-innovation-lab.html |access-date=2025-02-23 |website=BioSpectrum |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Goled |first=Shraddha |date=2020-09-24 |title=Wipro GE Healthcare Collaborates With IISc To Set Up AI Healthcare Innovation Lab |url=https://analyticsindiamag.com/ai-news-updates/wipro-ge-healthcare-collaborates-with-iisc-to-set-up-ai-healthcare-innovation-lab/ |access-date=2025-02-23 |website=Analytics India Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref>

With an emphasis on neurological disease diagnosis and population-level clinical impact analysis, [[Siemens Healthineers]] established the Computational Data Sciences Collaborative Laboratory for AI in Precision Medicine at [[IISc]] in 2024 to create [[Open source|open-source]] AI tools to automate the segmentation of pathological findings in neuroimaging data.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Pilla |first=Viswanath |date=2024-01-24 |title=Siemens Healthineers, IISc opens AI lab for precision medicine |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/healthcare/biotech/pharmaceuticals/siemens-healthineers-iisc-opens-ai-lab-for-precision-medicine/articleshow/107114377.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2025-02-23 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}</ref> 

As part of the Interdisciplinary Group for Advanced Research on Birth Outcomes – DBT India Initiative (GARBH-Ini) program, [[IIT Madras]] and [[Translational Health Science and Technology Institute]] in 2024 created India's first AI model, Garbhini-GA2, which will accurately estimate the age of the [[fetus]] in [[pregnant women]] in the [[Second trimester|second]] and [[Third trimester|third trimesters]]. In contrast to the current methods of determining a fetus's age in India, which use the Hadlock model developed using pregnancy data from Western countries or the more recent INTERGROWTH-21st model, the Garbhini-GA2, which is specific to the Indian population, uses genetic algorithm-based methods for estimating [[gestational age]]. This model reduces the error by nearly three times. The study was carried out in collaboration with [[Pondicherry Institute of Medical Sciences]], [[Christian Medical College Vellore]], [[Safdarjung Hospital]], and Gurugram Civil Hospital. Following the completion of pan-India validation, Garbhini-GA2 will be implemented in clinics throughout the country.<ref>{{Cite web |date=26 February 2024 |title=IIT-M & THSTI develop first India-specific AI model to determine foetus age |url=https://www.biospectrumindia.com/news/91/24243/iit-m-thsti-develop-first-india-specific-ai-model-to-determine-foetus-age.html |access-date=2025-02-07 |website=BioSpectrum |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sivapriyan |first=ETB |date=26 February 2024 |title=IIT Madras researchers develop first India-specific AI model to determine age of foetus |url=https://www.deccanherald.com/science/iit-madras-researchers-develop-first-india-specific-ai-model-to-determine-age-of-foetus-2910363 |access-date=2025-02-07 |website=Deccan Herald |language=en}}</ref> The [[Ministry of Science and Technology (India)|Ministry of Science and Technology]]'s [[Department of Biotechnology]] provided financing for the research, with additional support from the Robert Bosch Centre for Data Science and Artificial Intelligence (IIT Madras) and the Centre for Integrative Biology and Systems Medicine (IIT Madras).<ref>{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=2024-02-26 |title=India-specific model to give accurate gestational age of foetus |url=https://www.thehindu.com/sci-tech/science/india-specific-model-to-give-accurate-gestational-age-of-foetus/article67888396.ece |access-date=2025-02-07 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-02-26 |title=IIT Madras, THSTI researchers develop first India-specific AI model for foetus age |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/education-today/news/story/iit-madras-thsti-researchers-develop-first-india-specific-ai-model-for-foetus-age-2507157-2024-02-26 |access-date=2025-02-07 |website=India Today |language=en}}</ref>

In order to support healthy aging, constructive lifestyle modifications, and psycho-social wellbeing, Wipro and the Centre for Brain Research at IISc partnered in May 2024 to create an AI-based personal care engine that will consider a person's past medical history, desired health state, and behavioral responses to offer personalized help with chronic disease prevention and treatment.<ref>{{Cite web |date=29 May 2024 |title=Wipro collaborates with Centre for Brain Research at IISc for AI-driven health behaviour innovations |url=https://www.biospectrumindia.com/news/100/24690/wipro-collaborates-with-centre-for-brain-research-at-iisc-for-ai-driven-health-behaviour-innovations.html |access-date=2025-02-23 |website=BioSpectrum |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2024-05-28 |title=Wipro teams up with Centre for Brain Research at IISc on AI-driven health behaviour innovations |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/information-tech/wipro-teams-up-with-centre-for-brain-research-at-iisc-on-ai-driven-health-behaviour-innovations/articleshow/110486795.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2025-02-23 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}</ref> Researchers from [[St. John's Medical College|St. John's Hospital]] and [[IIIT-B]] are focusing on using [[computer vision]] for early detection of [[autism]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=T.R |first=Jahnavi |date=2024-11-21 |title=Researchers use computer vision for early detection of autism |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/bangalore/researchers-use-computer-vision-for-early-detection-of-autism/article68894133.ece |access-date=2025-02-19 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref>

=== Mobility ===
In an effort to improve road safety and decrease fatalities by half, [[Minister of Road Transport and Highways]] [[Nitin Gadkari]] inaugurated Intelligent Solutions for Road Safety through Technology and Engineering (iRASTE) under Mission Zero on 11 September 2021. The pilot project will run for two years in [[Nagpur]]. [[Intel]], [[International Institute of Information Technology, Hyderabad]], [[Central Road Research Institute]], [[Mahindra & Mahindra]], and [[Nagpur Municipal Corporation]] are part of the pilot project. It is focusing on vehicle safety, mobility analysis, and infrastructure safety.<ref>{{Cite web |title=iRASTE |url=https://inai.iiit.ac.in/iraste-telangana.html |access-date=2025-02-07 |website=inai.iiit.ac.in}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Gandharv |first=kumar |date=2021-09-13 |title=Nitin Gadkari Launches AI-Powered iRASTE Project For Road Safety |url=https://analyticsindiamag.com/ai-news-updates/nitin-gadkari-launches-ai-powered-iraste-project-for-road-safety/ |access-date=2025-02-18 |website=Analytics India Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref>

To improve vehicle safety, [[Nagpur Municipal Corporation|NMC]] will outfit its fleet of vehicles with [[Advanced driver-assistance system|advanced driver-assistance systems]] and [[Collision avoidance system|collision avoidance systems]]. They will also be equipped with sensors which will continuously monitor the road network's dynamic risks for mobility analysis, mapping the city into three zones: white (normal), grey (accident could happen), and black (accident has already happened). The data will be gathered by Intel AI Center at [[IIIT-H]] for monitoring and fixing the grey and black zones.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Deshpande |first=Vivek |date=2021-09-11 |title=With aim to enhance road safety in Nagpur, Nitin Gadkari launches iRASTE initiative |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/india/with-aim-to-enhance-road-safety-in-nagpur-nitin-gadkari-launches-iraste-initiative-7501907/ |access-date=2025-02-07 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=iRASTE project aims reducing road accidents, finding factors responsible: Intel India head |url=https://www.deccanherald.com/business/iraste-project-aims-reducing-road-accidents-finding-factors-responsible-intel-india-head-1029918.html |access-date=2025-02-07 |website=Deccan Herald |language=en}}</ref>

MINRO at IIIT-B is working on traffic analysis of Indian road conditions, analyzing traffic data, and using data for multimodal transport to make recommendations about the locations of  [[Urban rail transit in India|rail transit]] and [[Bus station|bus stations]].<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last=Kannaiah |first=Venkatesh |date=2024-03-25 |title=Our work on building 5G-Advanced base stations will be a game changer: Debabrata Das, Director, IIIT Bangalore |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/technology/tech-news-technology/5g-advanced-base-stations-will-be-a-game-changer-debabrata-das-director-iiit-bangalore-9230265/ |access-date=2025-02-19 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}}</ref>

=== Government ===
In 2021, the [[Ministry of Corporate Affairs]] introduced the first phase of MCA21 V3.0. It will allow for the electronic filing of documents under the [[corporate law]] and public access to corporate information. AI will be utilized by the platform to gather, organize, and classify stakeholder comments and inputs and produce analytical reports that will facilitate speedy policy choices.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2021-05-24 |title=Corporate Affairs Ministry launches first phase of MCA21 V3.0 portal |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/economy/policy/corporate-affairs-ministry-launches-first-phase-of-mca21-v3-0-portal/articleshow/82910166.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2025-02-08 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}</ref>

With assistance from [[Google]], the [[Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare]] and the [[Wadhwani Institute for Artificial Intelligence]] created Krishi 24/7, the first AI-powered automated agricultural news monitoring and analysis tool. Through better decision-making, Krishi 24/7 will support the identification of valuable news, provide timely notifications, and respond quickly to safeguard farmers' interests and advance sustainable agricultural growth. The application converts news articles into English after scanning them in several languages. It ensures that the ministry is informed in a timely manner about pertinent occurrences that are published online by extracting key information from news items, including the headline, crop name, event type, date, location, severity, summary, and source link. The [[National Centre for Disease Control|National Center for Disease Control]] has effectively implemented a comparable automated surveillance and analysis tool for disease outbreaks.<ref>{{Cite news |date=6 November 2023 |title=Krishi 24/7, the first-ever AI-powered solution for automated agricultural news monitoring and analysis |url=https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1975109 |access-date=13 April 2025 |work=[[Press Information Bureau]] |agency=Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India.}}</ref>

As part of the Safe City initiative, 1,000 AI cameras with [[Facial recognition system|facial recognition]] were placed at a cost of ₹96 [[crore]] in [[Lucknow]]'s commercial districts, colleges, hostels, large crossings, and public gathering spots. By integrating with the [[National Crime Records Bureau#National Automated Fingerprint Identification System|National Automated Fingerprint Identification System]], the cameras will detect suspicious movement of individuals by comparing their faces to a police database, notify control rooms of any criminal activities, and send out alerts against [[illegal dumping]]. For a more responsive and linked security network, AI will be included into [[Crisis hotline|crisis hotlines]] and [[Helpline|helplines]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2024-02-09 |title=In a 1st, 1K AI-enabled cameras to keep Lucknow safe and clean |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/lucknow/aienabled-cams-for-city-safety-and-cleanliness/articleshow/107542349.cms |access-date=2025-02-24 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref>

In collaboration with the [[Indian government]], IIIT-B created Datalake, a tool that analyzes government data on a range of projects to determine whether the objectives of the policy have been fulfilled and whether there is room for improvement. It can forecast how to modify the beneficiary structure to comply with the policy and benefit the citizens.<ref name=":4" />

The [[Government of Uttar Pradesh]] used [[Facial recognition system|facial recognition]] and AI-powered crowd density monitoring, RFID wristbands as part of the security setup for the [[2025 Prayag Maha Kumbh Mela]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=29 December 2024 |title=Maha Kumbh 2025: A Seamless and Spiritually Enriching Journey Awaits Devotees |url=https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2088675 |access-date=24 February 2025 |work=Press Information Bureau |agency=Ministry of Culture, Government of India}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=2024-12-30 |title=U.P. government to use AI-enabled cameras, RFID wristbands to track pilgrims at Mahakumbh |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/uttar-pradesh/up-government-to-use-ai-enabled-cameras-rfid-wristbands-to-track-pilgrims-at-mahakumbh/article69043950.ece |access-date=2025-02-24 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref> Plans to establish India's first AI lab aimed at strengthening cyber surveillance operations against [[deepfake]] threats and the country’s first tea auction driven by [[blockchain]] and AI, were announced by the [[Assam Government|Assam government]] in the state budget for 2025–2026.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kalita |first=Prabin |date=2025-03-10 |title=With Rs 2.6L-cr budget, Assam launches satellite plans, green & AI innovation |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/guwahati/with-rs-2-6l-cr-budget-assam-launches-satellite-plans-green-ai-innovation/articleshow/118856827.cms |access-date=2025-03-15 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref> It will focus on real-time online threat detection, [[digital forensics]], and cybersecurity. The lab will track cyberthreats, and assess misleading media.<ref>{{Cite web |date=10 March 2025 |title=Assam To Set Up India's First AI-Powered Anti-Deepfake & Cyber Surveillance Lab |url=https://www.guwahatiplus.com/assam/assam-to-set-up-indias-first-ai-powered-anti-deepfake-cyber-surveillance-lab |access-date=2025-03-15 |website=guwahatiplus.com |language=en}}</ref>

The AI Competency Framework was unveiled on 6 March 2025 by [[Ashwini Vaishnaw]], the [[Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology|Minister for Electronics and information Technology]], in recognition of the crucial role AI plays in governance. Its goal is to provide public sector professionals with the necessary skills for upskilling programs and AI competency mapping. This framework guarantees informed AI policy-making and implementation by conforming to international best practices. To improve government officials' iGOT Karmayogi platform learning experience, a tailored content suggestion system driven by AI was also unveiled.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":15" />  

=== Society ===
[[Wadhwani Institute for Artificial Intelligence|Wadhwani AI]], a $30 million nonprofit research institute, was established in 2018 by [[Romesh Wadhwani]] and [[Sunil Wadhwani]] with the goal of enhancing the lives of the world's poorest 2 billion people. [[New York University]], the [[University of Southern California]], [[Indian Institutes of Technology|India Institutes of Technology]], and [[University of Mumbai]] will collaborate with the institute. The objective is to have solutions that show how AI can help the [[underprivileged]], and then to build on those initial instances. Wadhwani AI will support universities from [[developing nations]] in expanding their AI capabilities.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cheney |first=Catherine |date=2018-02-21 |title=Indian billionaire brothers launch AI development research institute |url=https://www.devex.com/news/indian-billionaire-brothers-launch-ai-development-research-institute-92168 |access-date=2025-02-18 |website=Devex |language=en}}</ref> 

As part of [[Microsoft]]'s Global Skills for Social Impact charter, the ADVANTA(I)GE India program's first phase trained 2.4 million people in AI skills between 2024 and 2025; 74% of these persons came from [[Tier 2 cities in india|tier 2]] and [[Classification of Indian cities|tier 3]] cities, and 65% of them were women. Another 10 million people will be trained by 2030 as part of the second phase.<ref name=":16" /><ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2024-02-07 |title=Microsoft to provide AI skilling opportunities to 2 million people in India by 2025 |url=https://news.microsoft.com/en-in/microsoft-to-provide-ai-skilling-opportunities-to-2-million-people-in-india-by-2025/ |access-date=2025-06-05 |website=Microsoft |language=en-IN}}</ref>

The [[Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology]] launched '''IndiaAI Application Development Initiative''' on 6 March 2025. The aim is to create, scale, and encourage the usage of AI to improve the socioeconomic landscape of the country. In order to solve issues in the fields of healthcare, agriculture, governance, [[Climate change in India|climate change]], [[Disaster management in India|disaster management]], and [[learning disabilities]], IndiaAI has initiated the '''IndiaAI''' '''Innovation Challenge'''. Enhancing access to public services, improving healthcare, increasing agricultural productivity, helping people with learning disabilities, and lessening the effects of climate change are the goals. With the goal of lowering entry barriers in the field of AI, the '''IndiaAI FutureSkills Initiative''' will expand the number of AI courses offered in undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral level. To deliver foundational level training, IndiaAI Data Labs are being set up in [[Tier 2 cities in india|tier 2]] and [[Classification of Indian cities|tier 3]] locations throughout the country. IndiaAI has created the two courses for the positions of Data Curator and Data Annotator, with an emphasis on industries like manufacturing, healthcare, education, and agriculture. These will be taught in IndiaAI Data Labs located throughout 28 centers of the [[National Institute of Electronics & Information Technology]], and [[Industrial training institute|industrial training institutes]].<ref name=":14" /><ref>{{Cite news |date=19 March 2025 |title=Government of India Expands AI-Driven Skilling |url=https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2113095 |access-date=4 June 2025 |work=[[Press Information Bureau]] |agency=Ministry of Electronics & IT, Government of India.}}</ref>

== Safety and regulation ==
In order to determine whether to create an [[AI Safety Institute]] (AISI) that can establish standards, frameworks, and guidelines for AI development without serving as a regulatory body or stifling innovation, [[MeitY]] conducted consultation process with [[Meta Platforms]], [[Google]], [[Microsoft]], [[IBM]], [[OpenAI]], [[NASSCOM]], Broadband India Forum, [[Software Alliance]], [[Indian Institutes of Technology]], The Quantum Hub, Digital Empowerment Foundation, and [[Access Now]] on 7 October 2024. It was decided that instead of focusing on regulation, the AISI would focus on damage detection, risk identification, and standards setting for which interoperable systems are necessary to prevent the development of silos which may eventually influence future policies. The Safe and Trusted Pillar of the IndiaAI Mission has been allocated [[₹]]20 [[crore]], which the AISI may use for the inaugural budget. More money from the IndiaAI Mission's other verticals may be used in the future.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2024-10-13 |title=Govt mulls setting up Artificial Intelligence Safety Institute |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/govt-mulls-setting-up-artificial-intelligence-safety-institute-101728833433153.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241120105636/https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/govt-mulls-setting-up-artificial-intelligence-safety-institute-101728833433153.html |archive-date=2024-11-20 |access-date=2025-02-17 |work=Hindustan Times |language=en-us}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Jeevanandam |first=Nivash |date=15 October 2024 |title=MeitY Hosts Consultation for Establishing India AI Safety Institute under IndiaAI Mission's Safe and Trusted Pillar |url=https://indiaai.gov.in/news/meity-hosts-consultation-for-establishing-india-ai-safety-institute-under-indiaai-mission-s-safe-and-trusted-pillar |access-date=2025-02-17 |website=IndiaAI |language=en}}</ref>

In order to develop an AI policy report tailored to India and assess the country's AI ecosystem's strengths and future prospects, [[UNESCO]] and MeitY began consulting on AI Readiness Assessment Methodology under Safety and Ethics in Artificial Intelligence from 2024. It is to encourage the ethical and responsible use of AI in industries. The study will help find areas where government can become involved, especially in attempts to strengthen institutional and regulatory capabilities.<ref>{{Cite news |date=16 November 2024 |title=UNESCO and the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, Host Multi-Stakeholder Consultation on Safety and Ethics in Artificial Intelligence |url=https://pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2073920 |access-date=19 February 2025 |work=[[Press Information Bureau]] |agency=Ministry of Electronics & IT, Government of India}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=21 January 2025 |title=UNESCO and Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) host stakeholder consultation on AI Readiness Assessment Methodology (RAM) in India |url=https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2094899 |access-date=19 February 2025 |work=[[Press Information Bureau]] |agency=Ministry of Electronics & IT, Government of India}}</ref>

[[Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology|Minister for Electronics & Information Technology]] [[Ashwini Vaishnaw]] announced the creation of an [[IndiaAI Safety Institute]] on 30 January 2025, to ensure the ethical and safe application of AI models. The institute will promote domestic [[research and development]] that is grounded in India's social, economic, cultural, and linguistic diversity and is based on Indian datasets. With the help of academic and research institutions, as well as private sector partners, the institute will follow the [[hub-and-spoke]] approach to carry out projects within Safe and Trusted Pillar of the IndiaAI Mission. Among the major safety-related initiatives are eight ongoing projects to implement a techno-legal strategy to protect data privacy while conducting an ethical audit of algorithmic effectiveness.<ref name=":5" />

[[Infosys]] released an open-source "Responsible AI" toolbox on 26 February 2025. The program, is a component of the Infosys Topaz Responsible AI Suite. It assists in identifying and stopping security risks, privacy violations, biased outputs, damaging content, copyright infringement, false information, deepfakes, and the use of malevolent AI. The toolkit can improve the transparency of outcomes produced by AI. It works with both on-premises and cloud systems.<ref>{{Cite web |date=26 February 2025 |title=Infosys Unveils Open Source 'Responsible AI' Toolkit To Promote Ethical Use |url=https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/infosys-unveils-open-source-responsible-ai-toolkit-to-promote-ethical-use-7799415 |access-date=2025-02-27 |website=ndtv.com |language=en}}</ref> Citing concerns about the confidentiality of government data and documents, the [[Ministry of Finance (India)|Ministry of Finance]] issued an internal department caution advising staff not to use AI tools like [[ChatGPT]] and [[DeepSeek (chatbot)|DeepSeek]] for work-related purposes.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Singh |first1=Sarita |last2=Ohri |first2=Nikunj |date=5 February 2025 |title=India's finance ministry asks employees to avoid AI tools like ChatGPT, DeepSeek |url=https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/indias-finance-ministry-asks-employees-avoid-ai-tools-like-chatgpt-deepseek-2025-02-05/ |access-date=3 March 2025 |work=[[Reuters]]}}</ref> 

In order to comply with the [[Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023]] and other sovereignty requirements, [[OpenAI]] allowed the local storage of data for ChatGPT Enterprise, ChatGPT Edu, and OpenAI [[API]] platform customers from 8 May 2025.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Aryan |first=Aashish |date=8 May 2025 |title=OpenAI to store ChatGPT Enterprise and API user data locally in India |url=https://www.business-standard.com/technology/tech-news/openai-chatgpt-india-data-residency-enterprise-edu-api-launch-125050800140_1.html |access-date=12 June 2025 |work=[[Business Standard]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Lohchab |first=Himanshi |date=2025-05-20 |title=ET Explainer: What OpenAI's local data residency means for India |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/artificial-intelligence/et-explainer-what-openais-local-data-residency-means-for-india/articleshow/121275267.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2025-06-12 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}</ref> Talks to establish data center operations in India have already been started by OpenAI.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Aryan |first=Aashish |date=13 February 2025 |title=ChatGPT maker OpenAI's plan to set up India data centre in the works |url=https://www.business-standard.com/technology/tech-news/chatgpt-maker-openai-s-plan-to-set-up-india-data-centre-in-the-works-125021301533_1.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250220163942/https://www.business-standard.com/technology/tech-news/chatgpt-maker-openai-s-plan-to-set-up-india-data-centre-in-the-works-125021301533_1.html |archive-date=2025-02-20 |access-date=2025-06-12 |website=Business Standard |language=en-US}}</ref> 

[[Google]] launched its Safety Charter for India's AI-led transformation on 18 June 2025. Keeping end users safe, cybersecurity for government and enterprise infrastructure, and responsibly developing AI are the three core pillars that it outlines for addressing the difficulties of the online world in partnership with the larger ecosystem.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mishra |first=Urvashi |date=2025-06-18 |title=Google unveils Safety Charter to secure India's AI-powered digital future |url=https://www.fortuneindia.com/technology/google-unveils-safety-charter-to-secure-indias-ai-powered-digital-future/124147 |access-date=2025-06-20 |website=Fortune India |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Jain |first=Ayushi |date=2025-06-17 |title=As AI grows, Google introduces Safety Charter in India to fight scams and boost cybersecurity |url=https://www.digit.in/news/general/as-ai-grows-google-rolls-out-safety-charter-in-india-to-fight-scams-and-boost-cybersecurity.html |access-date=2025-06-20 |website=Digit |language=en}}</ref> In order to operationalize Google's Safety Charter, Google Safety Engineering Center in [[Hyderabad]] was established.<ref>{{Cite web |last=John |first=Merin Susan |date=2025-06-19 |title=Google Opens Cybersecurity Hub in Hyderabad to Strengthen India's Digital Safety Infra |url=https://analyticsindiamag.com/ai-news-updates/google-opens-cybersecurity-hub-in-hyderabad-to-strengthen-indias-digital-safety-infra/ |access-date=2025-06-20 |website=Analytics India Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref>

The artificial intelligence (AI) market in India is projected to reach $8 billion by 2025, growing at 40% CAGR from 2020 to 2025. This growth is part of the broader AI boom, a global period of rapid technological advancements with India being pioneer starting in the early 2010s with NLP based Chatbots from Haptik, Corover.ai, Niki.ai and then gaining prominence in the early 2020s based on reinforcement learning, marked by breakthroughs such as generative AI models from Krutrim, Sarvam, CoRover, OpenAI and Alphafold by Google DeepMind. In India, the development of AI has been similarly transformative, with applications in healthcare, finance, and education, bolstered by government initiatives like NITI Aayog's 2018 National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence. Institutions such as the Indian Statistical Institute and the Indian Institute of Science published breakthrough AI research papers and patents. 
India's transformation to AI is primarily being driven by startups and government initiatives & policies like Digital India. By fostering technological trust through digital public infrastructure, India is tackling socioeconomic issues by taking a bottom-up approach to AI. NASSCOM and Boston Consulting Group estimate that by 2027, India's AI services might be valued at $17 billion. According to 2025 Technology and Innovation Report, by UN Trade and Development, India ranks 10th globally for private sector investments in AI. According to Mary Meeker, India has emerged as a key market for AI platforms, accounting for the largest share of ChatGPT's mobile app users and having the third-largest user base for DeepSeek in 2025.
While AI presents significant opportunities for economic growth and social development in India, challenges such as data privacy concerns, skill shortages, and ethical considerations need to be addressed for responsible AI deployment. The growth of AI in India has also led to an increase in the number of cyberattacks that use AI to target organizations.
